'''Elmer William Colglazier''' (born November 24, 1944) is an American physicist, best known as the fourth science and technology adviser to the [[United States Secretary of State|U.S. Secretary of State]] from 2011 to 2014. In that role, he has written about the benefits of [[science diplomacy]].<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Colglazier|first1=E. William|title=The United States Looks to the Global Science, Technology, and Innovation Horizon|journal=Science & Diplomacy|date=July 8, 2014|volume=3|issue=3|url=http://www.sciencediplomacy.org/perspective/2014/united-states-looks-global-science-technology-and-innovation-horizon}}</ref>

Colglazier received his Ph.D. in theoretical physics from the [[California Institute of Technology]] in 1971. He then worked at the [[Stanford Linear Accelerator Center]], the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in Princeton, and the Center for Science and International Affairs at Harvard's [[Kennedy School of Government]]. While at Harvard, he also served as associate director of the Program in Science, Technology, and Humanism of the [[Aspen Institute]]. In 1976 and 1977, he was an AAAS Congressional Science Fellow working for Congressman [[George Brown, Jr.|George Brown]].<ref name="state">U.S. Department of State, [https://web.archive.org/web/20111031022951/http://www.state.gov/r/pa/ei/biog/169019.htm "Biography: E. William Colglazier"]</ref>

From 1983 to 1991, he was professor of physics and director of the Energy, Environment, and Resources Center at the [[University of Tennessee]], where he worked closely with scientists at [[Oak Ridge National Laboratory]]. From 1991 to 1994, Colglazier was executive director of the Office of International Affairs of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] (NAS) and [[National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine|National Academies of Sciences]] (NRC).<ref name="state" />

From 1994 to 2011, Colglazier served as executive officer of the NAS and NRC. From 2000 to 2011, he also served as NRC's chief operating officer.<ref name="state" />

Colglazier has been married to Catherine Clark Colglazier, former teacher and Humanities Manager at [[Thomas Jefferson High School for Science and Technology]] in [[Alexandria, Virginia]] for 50 years. They have two married children: Geraldine Tunnell, Senior VP for Marketing at Dell, and Will Colglazier, US History teacher at Aragon High School (CA). He resides in McLean, VA.{{Citation needed|date=August 2022}}
